entries.title: II Samuel 14:1
segments: ¶Now Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king's heart [was] toward Absalom.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:2
segments: And Joab sent to Tekoah, and fetched thence a wise woman, and said unto her, I pray thee, feign thyself to be a mourner, and put on now mourning apparel, and anoint not thyself with oil, but be as a woman that had a long time mourned for the dead:

words.text: unto her, I pray thee, feign thyself to be a mourner

entries.title: II Samuel 14:3
segments: And come to the king, and speak on this manner unto him. So Joab put the words in her mouth.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:4
segments: And when the woman of Tekoah spake to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, and did obeisance, and said, Help, O king. {Help: Heb. Save}

entries.title: II Samuel 14:5
segments: And the king said unto her, What aileth thee? And she answered, I [am] indeed a widow woman, and mine husband is dead.

words.text: unto her, What aileth thee? And she answered

entries.title: II Samuel 14:6
segments: And thy handmaid had two sons, and they two strove together in the field, and [there was] none to part them, but the one smote the other, and slew him. {none...: Heb. no deliverer between them}

entries.title: II Samuel 14:7
segments: And, behold, the whole family is risen against thine handmaid, and they said, Deliver him that smote his brother, that we may kill him, for the life of his brother whom he slew; and we will destroy the heir also: and so they shall quench my coal which is left, and shall not leave to my husband [neither] name nor remainder upon the earth. {upon...: Heb. upon the face of the earth}

entries.title: II Samuel 14:8
segments: And the king said unto the woman, Go to thine house, and I will give charge concerning thee.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:9
segments: And the woman of Tekoah said unto the king, My lord, O king, the iniquity [be] on me, and on my father's house: and the king and his throne [be] guiltless.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:12
segments: Then the woman said, Let thine handmaid, I pray thee, speak [one] word unto my lord the king. And he said, Say on.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:13
segments: And the woman said, Wherefore then hast thou thought such a thing against the people of God? for the king doth speak this thing as one which is faulty, in that the king doth not fetch home again his banished.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:14
segments: For we must needs die, and [are] as water spilt on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again; neither doth God respect [any] person: yet doth he devise means, that his banished be not expelled from him. {neither...: or, because God hath not taken away his life, he hath also devised means, etc}

entries.title: II Samuel 14:15
segments: Now therefore that I am come to speak of this thing unto my lord the king, [it is] because the people have made me afraid: and thy handmaid said, I will now speak unto the king; it may be that the king will perform the request of his handmaid.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:16
segments: For the king will hear, to deliver his handmaid out of the hand of the man [that would] destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:17
segments: Then thine handmaid said, The word of my lord the king shall now be comfortable: for as an angel of God, so [is] my lord the king to discern good and bad: therefore the LORD thy God will be with thee. {comfortable: Heb. for rest} {to discern: Heb. to hear}

words.text: will be with thee. {comfortable: Heb. for rest} {to discern: Heb. to hear}

entries.title: II Samuel 14:18
segments: Then the king answered and said unto the woman, Hide not from me, I pray thee, the thing that I shall ask thee. And the woman said, Let my lord the king now speak.

words.text: not from me, I pray thee, the thing

entries.title: II Samuel 14:19
segments: And the king said, [Is not] the hand of Joab with thee in all this? And the woman answered and said, [As] thy soul liveth, my lord the king, none can turn to the right hand or to the left from ought that my lord the king hath spoken: for thy servant Joab, he bade me, and he put all these words in the mouth of thine handmaid:

words.text: with thee in all this? And the woman

entries.title: II Samuel 14:20
segments: To fetch about this form of speech hath thy servant Joab done this thing: and my lord [is] wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all [things] that [are] in the earth.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:21
segments: ¶And the king said unto Joab, Behold now, I have done this thing: go therefore, bring the young man Absalom again.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:22
segments: And Joab fell to the ground on his face, and bowed himself, and thanked the king: and Joab said, To day thy servant knoweth that I have found grace in thy sight, my lord, O king, in that the king hath fulfilled the request of his servant. {thanked: Heb. blessed} {his servant: or, thy servant}

entries.title: II Samuel 14:23
segments: So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:24
segments: And the king said, Let him turn to his own house, and let him not see my face. So Absalom returned to his own house, and saw not the king's face.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:25
segments: But in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him. {But...: Heb. And as Absalom there was not a beautiful man in all Israel to praise greatly}

entries.title: II Samuel 14:26
segments: And when he polled his head, (for it was at every year's end that he polled [it]: because [the hair] was heavy on him, therefore he polled it:) he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels after the king's weight.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:27
segments: And unto Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter, whose name [was] Tamar: she was a woman of a fair countenance.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:28
segments: ¶So Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem, and saw not the king's face.

segments: Therefore Absalom sent for Joab, to have sent him to the king; but he would not come to him: and when he sent again the second time, he would not come.
